text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper presents a non-review research study focused on the development and application of LUCAS, a spatially explicit state-and-transition simulation model for predicting future land use and land cover (LULC) change across the conterminous United States—a national-scale domain. The model implements multiple future scenarios (e.g., IPCC-SRES A1B, A2, B1, B2; RCPs; historical extrapolations), satisfying the ≥2 scenario requirement. It produces mapped LULC projections at 1-km resolution and includes quantitative outputs such as area targets, transition probabilities, net change statistics by ecoregion (Table 4), and verification metrics (R² > 0.99 in Figure 6). The primary objective is LULC prediction integrated with carbon dynamics, but LULC change is central to the modeling framework and not merely an input. All core inclusion criteria are met, and none of the exclusion criteria apply—despite the carbon focus, LULC change is explicitly modeled, spatially allocated, and analyzed under multiple future scenarios at the national scale.)
